## Overview

This chart is built around the Life Palace in the You 酉 (You) branch, holding Tian Tong (the easygoing helper and comfort-seeker, a star of kindness, modest ambition and contentment) at neutral brightness, with Huo Xing (a fast, sparking challenging star) also in the palace. The Body Palace sits in the same palace as the Life Palace, which is a strong statement: what you see on the surface and what drives you underneath are closely aligned. You tend to be recognizably yourself in most rooms — steady, agreeable, not especially showy, but with a quicker temper or restless impulse tucked inside that gentler exterior.

The Five Element Bureau is Wood 3, which traditionally gives a growing, branching, upward-reaching temperament: things develop gradually and organically rather than in sudden bursts, and your best progress often comes from patient cultivation rather than force. Two distinctive traits stand out across the whole chart. First, a strong pull toward ease and harmony (Tian Tong in the Life Palace) paired with a busy inner spark (Huo Xing), which means you often need to deliberately choose challenge rather than wait to feel motivated. Second, a chart unusually rich in transformation meaning: Po Jun (the pioneer who clears the old to build the new) carries birth-year Hua Lu (prosperity) in the Property Palace, Ju Men (the reasoned debater, a star of speech and analysis) carries Hua Quan (power) in the Wealth Palace, Tai Yin (the gentle moon, a star of refinement and quiet planning) carries Hua Ke (recognition) in the Travel Palace, and Tan Lang (the charismatic seeker of experience) carries Hua Ji (obstacle, needs extra care) in the Health Palace. Much of your life story runs through property, money, travel and health rather than through romance or fame.

For a newcomer: the Life Palace is the anchor of the chart — the palace describing your core temperament and the way you meet the world. The Body Palace describes where your energy actually lands later in life, the part of you that acts rather than observes. Here they coincide, so there is little gap between intention and behaviour.

## Life Palace and Personality

Tian Tong at neutral brightness in the Life Palace suggests a fundamentally friendly, accommodating nature with a taste for comfort, good food, good company and a low-conflict environment. It is a star that prefers to smooth things over rather than win. At neutral rather than brilliant brightness, its ease can shade into inertia: you might let a situation drift because addressing it feels unpleasant. The supporting Huo Xing in the same palace supplies the counterweight — a sharp, impatient spark that surfaces when pushed, and that gives you more drive than the placid surface suggests. Working with this combination means building small, timed challenges into your life (a deadline, a class, a commitment to someone else) so the Huo Xing energy has somewhere constructive to go, rather than accumulating into sudden irritation.

Because the Body Palace is in the same palace, there's a consistency to you that others find reassuring, and a risk that you stay in the same groove for too long. You are unlikely to reinvent your manner; the growth happens in what you do, not in who you appear to be. The Travel Palace opposite carries Tai Yin at fallen brightness with birth-year Hua Ke (recognition) and the auspicious You Bi and Tian Kui — so recognition and helpful people often arrive through movement, travel and unfamiliar settings rather than at home. Stepping out of your usual environment tends to bring out a more capable, more visible version of you.

## Career

The Career Palace in Chou 丑 (Chou) holds Tian Ji (the strategist, a star of planning, calculation and resourcefulness) at fallen brightness, with the challenging Qing Yang alongside it. Tian Ji at fallen brightness points to a mind that works hard on plans but can overthink, revise and second-guess; Qing Yang adds a cutting, decisive edge that can tip either into crisp execution or into friction with colleagues. The practical read is that you do best in roles with genuine problem-solving and room to redesign the approach — analysis, operations, planning, process improvement — while keeping the scope of your planning tight, because Tian Ji's tendency is to keep computing past the point of usefulness.

The opposite palace, the Spouse Palace, holds Tian Liang (the elder advisor, a star of principle and sound judgement) at bright brightness, which suggests that a partner or close ally can be an excellent sounding board for career decisions, and that collaboration with someone more senior or more settled than you steadies your choices. Support arrives indirectly rather than from a formal mentor structure.

Worth watching: Qing Yang in the Career Palace rewards directness but punishes sharpness. Aim your decisiveness at problems, not people.

## Wealth

The Wealth Palace in Si 巳 (Si) holds Ju Men (the reasoned debater, associated with speech, analysis and argument) at bright brightness with birth-year Hua Quan (power), plus the auspicious Tian Yue. This is a strong money palace: Ju Men with Hua Quan suggests earning power that comes through voice, persuasion, expertise and the ability to argue a case clearly — negotiation, teaching, consulting, writing, advocacy, sales of complex things. Tian Yue adds a softening, helpful-person quality, so opportunities often come through goodwill and introductions rather than cold approach. Because Ju Men is a star of words rather than of quiet accumulation, income tends to grow when you put your thinking and your explaining out in public.

The Spirit Palace opposite carries Tai Yang at fallen brightness with Zuo Fu plus the challenging Tuo Luo, Di Kong and Di Jie. That mix suggests that your inner sense of "enough" and your actual wealth can drift apart — delayed gratification (Tuo Luo) and a feeling of emptiness or dissatisfaction (Di Kong, Di Jie) can make you discount what you have, while Zuo Fu reassures that support and resourcefulness are present. The habit worth building is a regular, unemotional review of money: what came in, what went out, what you actually need. Hua Quan in the Wealth Palace can make you push hard for financial control; the challenge is to let the review be factual rather than a verdict on yourself.

## Love and Partnership

The Spouse Palace in Wei 未 (Wei) holds Tian Liang (the elder advisor) at bright brightness, with no challenging stars listed in the palace. Tian Liang in this position points toward a partner who is principled, steady, perhaps a little more traditional or more mature in outlook than you, and who functions as a stabilising voice. Bright brightness is a favourable sign here: the qualities of honesty and reliability are likely to be on show rather than buried. Because Tian Liang is a star of judgement rather than of high romance, the relationship tends to be built on respect, shared standards and practical support more than grand gestures — and that suits Tian Tong in your Life Palace, which wants peace and companionship over drama.

The opposite palace, the Career Palace, carries Tian Ji at fallen brightness with Qing Yang. This suggests that work pressure and work intensity can spill into the relationship, especially if you bring the strategising and the sharp edge home. It also suggests that shared projects — planning something together, solving something together — can be the channel through which closeness deepens.

With Huo Xing in the Life Palace, a quick flare of temper is possible in domestic moments. Naming it early ("I'm wound up, give me a minute") tends to work better for you than suppressing it, which is Tian Tong's default.

## Wellbeing Habits

The Health Palace in Chen 辰 (Chen) holds Tan Lang (the charismatic seeker of experience, a star of appetite and enjoyment) at brilliant brightness with birth-year Hua Ji (obstacle, needs extra care), plus the auspicious Wen Qu. Tan Lang is a star of indulgence, so food, drink and stimulating experience are areas where moderation asks for more attention than it does for most people; Hua Ji in this palace is a reminder to keep those appetites in view rather than on autopilot. Wen Qu in the same palace is a favourable counterweight: it points to learning, reading and structured knowledge as genuine supports, so educating yourself about your own patterns tends to pay off.

From the Life Palace, Tian Tong favours rest, warmth and regularity, while Huo Xing pushes bursts of intensity followed by crashes. The rhythm that suits you best is steadier rather than heroic: consistent sleep and wake times, meals at roughly the same hours, and movement that is moderate and frequent rather than occasional and extreme — a daily walk or a short, regular practice channels Huo Xing better than an occasional hard session. For emotional balance, Tian Tong benefits from having a small circle you can talk to honestly, since the tendency is to keep the peace by staying quiet. Hobbies that involve your hands or your senses, in the spirit of Tan Lang, give the appetite for enjoyment a healthy outlet.

If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Family and Social Circle

The Friends Palace in Yin 寅 (Yin) holds Zi Wei (the emperor, a star of authority and dignity) at bright brightness and Tian Fu (the treasurer, a star of stability and stored resources) at brilliant brightness — a notably strong combination. This points to a social circle containing capable, senior or well-established people who can open doors, and to you being respected among peers. The Siblings Palace opposite holds Qi Sha (the general, a star of decisive force) at brilliant brightness, which suggests siblings or close peers who are independent and strong-willed, sometimes abrasive. The dynamic to manage is letting strong characters be strong without turning every difference into a contest.

The Parents Palace in Xu 戌 (Xu) holds Wu Qu (the financier, a star of discipline and hard value) at brilliant brightness with the auspicious Wen Chang and the challenging Ling Xing. Wu Qu here suggests parents or elders who value achievement, practicality and getting things done; Wen Chang adds a scholarly, communicative quality; Ling Xing suggests occasional abruptness or a sharp edge in those relationships. The practical approach is to engage elders on concrete matters — a task, a plan, a piece of news — rather than on feelings, which flows more easily with Wu Qu and Wen Chang.

The Children Palace in Wu 午 (Wu) holds Lian Zhen (the charming operator, a star of social savvy and desire) at neutral brightness and Tian Xiang (the minister, a star of loyal service and poise) at brilliant brightness, with no challenging stars listed. With younger people or children in your life, expect independence and a strong sense of their own dignity; Tian Xiang responds well to being given responsibility and clear roles.

## Major Period and Year by Year

You are in the Major Period of the Career Palace (ages 43–52, about 2025–2034), in Chou 丑 (Chou), holding Tian Ji at fallen brightness with Qing Yang. This is a decade centred on work and on the mental labour of planning. Tian Ji at fallen brightness suggests a period of heavy strategising, revision and rethinking of your professional path, and Qing Yang gives it pace and decisiveness — good for cutting through stalled situations, but tiring if sustained without pause. The overall rhythm of these ten years is busy and analytical rather than expansive: the focus is on refining what you do and how you do it, with the reward arriving later. The absence of birth-year transformations in this palace means the decade's character comes from these two stars rather than from a strong luck-current of its own, so deliberate choices matter more here than momentum.

The Next Major Period moves to the Friends Palace (ages 53–62, about 2035–2044) in Yin 寅 (Yin), with Zi Wei at bright brightness and Tian Fu at brilliant brightness. That shift points toward a decade where networks, community and established alliances come to the fore — a broader, more socially anchored phase after this one's close professional focus.

Each annual pillar below follows the Chinese lunar year and roughly matches the calendar year.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu

The annual Life Palace falls on the Children Palace, with Lian Zhen at neutral brightness and Tian Xiang at brilliant brightness, so this year carries a flavour of social poise, enjoyable company and a sense of dignity in how you present yourself. Lian Zhen brings charm and appetite for experience; Tian Xiang brings composure and a sense of duty.

The year's Four Transformations: Hua Lu (prosperity) lands on Tian Tong in your natal Life Palace, a warm and favourable placement that supports ease, comfort and being well received. Hua Quan (power) lands on Tian Ji in the natal Career Palace, reinforcing the decade's professional drive — a good year to push a plan forward. Hua Ke (recognition) lands on Wen Chang in the natal Parents Palace, favouring study, writing and clear communication with elders or authority. Hua Ji (obstacle, needs extra care) lands on Lian Zhen in the natal Children Palace, which is also this year's annual Life Palace — so the area of pleasure and sociability is where care is needed: enjoy the company, but watch the appetite for more. Lean into the Life Palace's ease early in the year and put effort into work matters through the first half.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei

The annual Life Palace moves to the Spouse Palace, with Tian Liang at bright brightness — a year that foregrounds partnership, principled conduct and the steadying presence of others. The tone is calmer and more relational than the previous year.

Hua Lu (prosperity) lands on Tai Yin in the natal Travel Palace, favouring journeys, new settings and quiet planning done at a distance. Hua Quan (power) lands on Tian Tong in the natal Life Palace, giving you more personal authority and presence than usual — a good year to speak up for yourself. Hua Ke (recognition) lands on Tian Ji in the natal Career Palace, so professional recognition through careful work is well supported. Hua Ji (obstacle, needs extra care) lands on Ju Men in the natal Wealth Palace, so financial communication — terms, agreements, expectations about money — deserves a slower pace and clear wording. In the second half, a partnership conversation could be worth having unhurried.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen

The annual Life Palace moves to the Siblings Palace, with Qi Sha at brilliant brightness — an energetic, independent, forward-driving tone for the year. Qi Sha brings decisiveness and a willingness to act alone; it suits tackling something you've been circling.

Hua Lu (prosperity) lands on Tan Lang in the natal Health Palace, which favours enjoyment and vitality but also asks for moderation. Hua Quan (power) lands on Tai Yin in the natal Travel Palace, giving weight to plans and agreements made away from home. Hua Ke (recognition) lands on You Bi in the natal Travel Palace, so help from others tends to arrive through travel and new settings. Hua Ji (obstacle, needs extra care) lands on Tian Ji in the natal Career Palace — the strategic mind is under pressure this year, so resist over-planning and let some decisions rest. Pace yourself: Qi Sha's drive is real but it burns fuel.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You

The annual Life Palace returns to your natal Life Palace, with Tian Tong at neutral brightness — a year that feels like yourself, familiar and steady. It is a good year to consolidate rather than launch.

Hua Lu (prosperity) lands on Wu Qu in the natal Parents Palace, favouring practical support and goodwill from elders or authority figures. Hua Quan (power) lands on Tan Lang in the natal Health Palace, giving appetite and energy more force — channel it into structured activity. Hua Ke (recognition) lands on Tian Liang in the natal Spouse Palace, supporting honest, respectful partnership conversations. Hua Ji (obstacle, needs extra care) lands on Wen Qu in the natal Health Palace, which points to overthinking or mental strain affecting your rest: protect sleep and cut back on late-night screen work. Toward the end of the year, review what the year taught rather than starting something new.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu

The annual Life Palace moves to the Parents Palace, with Wu Qu at brilliant brightness, plus Wen Chang and Ling Xing — a year centred on elders, authority, structure and getting concrete things done, with a slightly sharp edge.

Hua Lu (prosperity) lands on Tai Yang in the natal Spirit Palace, favouring inner contentment and enjoyment of what you have. Hua Quan (power) lands on Wu Qu in the natal Parents Palace, which is also this year's annual Life Palace — decisiveness and practical authority are strongly supported. Hua Ke (recognition) lands on Tai Yin in the natal Travel Palace again, keeping travel and quiet planning well-starred. Hua Ji (obstacle, needs extra care) lands on Tian Tong in the natal Life Palace, so ease and comfort are harder to come by this year — build rest in deliberately rather than waiting for it. Lean into the practical; be gentle with the urge to keep the peace at your own expense.

## Guidance

- **Give Huo Xing in the Life Palace a daily outlet.** A short, timed burst of movement or a small challenge with a deadline keeps the spark constructive instead of letting it surface as sudden irritation.
- **Keep a plain, factual money review each season, sparked by Hua Quan on Ju Men in the Wealth Palace and tempered by Tuo Luo and Di Kong in the Spirit Palace.** Look at income, outgoings and what you actually need; treat it as information, not a judgement.
- **Send your thinking outward.** With Ju Men in the Wealth Palace and Hua Quan on it, writing, teaching, speaking or explaining your expertise publicly is well suited to how this chart earns.
- **Protect regular sleep and mealtimes, given Tan Lang with Hua Ji in the Health Palace and Tian Tong in the Life Palace.** Consistency suits you better than intensity; when Wen Qu is under Hua Ji in 2029, trim mental load toward the end of the year.
- **Use movement and unfamiliar settings for recognition, following Tai Yin with Hua Ke and the auspicious You Bi and Tian Kui in the Travel Palace.** Time away from your usual environment tends to bring out your more capable side and bring helpful people into view.
